items.answer: The iterative software development life cycle has three evaluation points: early evaluation, which quickly evaluates interface and interaction design ideas with fewer resources and less time as part of the design-prototype-evaluate cycle; code testing, which evaluates the code as part of coding and implementation; and empirical study.
Cognitive walkthrough is a quick expert evaluation technique and usability inspection method in which usability problems are identified by inspecting a prototype.

Heuristic evaluation is an evaluation technique in which evaluators assess a presented prototype by ticking items on a checklist of heuristics, without a task scenario or task performance, to perform a comprehensive evaluation of the whole system rather than a task-specific evaluation.
The tracking process broadly consists of four steps: calibration, registration, integration, and drift correction.

In an Extended Reality (XR) system, interaction design and modeling, which relate to input and give the user ease of interacting with the system, and perceptual design and modeling, which relate to output and make the output appropriately sensed, understood, or perceived by the user, are both important for usability.

The design-prototype-evaluate loop refines early designs for interactive systems using user feedback through many iterations, in which a design is prototyped, evaluated to identify problems, and refined until not many significantly different problems are identified, after which the design is stabilized and the next stage can begin.
